description: The non-regression oracle shared by both SDKs. Every positive value of content-cleaning-vectors.json is written between each `prefixes` entry and each `suffixes` entry (see `placement`), and every string input of its cases is taken as it is; each text is cleaned by the reference engine (testdata/reference-engine/, frozen) and by the engine under test. Whatever the reference masked must still be masked: the engine under test may mask more, never less, except where one of the closed list of `exclusions` stands. Edited by hand.
placement: A lead that ends with a character other than a blank, with = or : and blanks, or with the word Bearer or Basic and a space, is part of the value's form (postgres://, Email:, AccountKey = , Authorization: Bearer): the prefix goes before it. A trail that starts with @ or : is too (the @host of a connection string): the suffix goes after it. Otherwise the prefix and the suffix stand right next to the value. Texts are taken in order (positives, then prefixes, then suffixes), the first occurrence of a text for a detector only.

floor.description: The neutral contexts: written around a positive value as `placement` says, each must leave the value counted by its detector, under a policy enabling that detector alone. A context in which the detector counts nothing is a failure, not a pass.

exclusions.name: version_word
exclusions.reason: Four numbers right after an unambiguous version word (version, ver., release, firmware, revision, release- included) are a version number, not an address.

exclusions.name: git_remote
exclusions.reason: user@host:path right after git clone, git remote add or set-url, scp or rsync is a remote, not an address.

exclusions.name: git_user
exclusions.reason: The user git alone before the host of a URL (ssh://git@host) names a service, not a credential.

exclusions.name: escape_letter
exclusions.reason: The letter of an escape written in two characters (\n, \t, \r) right before an address is the escape's, not the address's: the address starts after it.

exclusions.name: escape_shift
exclusions.reason: Behind an escape written in two characters the reference could not read a card's first group, and read a shifted card from the second group on, digits after it included; the engine reads the card itself, and what follows it is not part of it.

exclusions.name: image_name
exclusions.reason: An image name at a pixel density (logo@2x.png) is a file name, not an address.

exclusions.name: round_amount
exclusions.reason: Round thousands after a plus sign (+150 000 000, +12 500 000) are a quantity, not a number.

exclusions.name: quoted_key_header
exclusions.reason: A private key's BEGIN line with no key material right after it (a word of prose, a parenthesis, another BEGIN line, fewer than 32 base64 characters) is quoted, not a key: the reference masked it, or everything after it when 32 base64 characters stood anywhere in the next 1,024 (a commit hash, a long path). It is now left as it is under Mask and blocks under Block.

exclusions.name: variable_reference_password
exclusions.reason: A reference to a variable in braces (${NAME}) as the password or token of a URL is a name, not a secret: the reference masked it with the user before it; it is now left as it is, as it already was in an assignment.

exclusions.name: variable_reference_url
exclusions.reason: A reference to a variable in braces (${NAME}) as the password or token of a URL is a name, not a secret: the reference masked it with the user before it; it is now left as it is, as it already was in an assignment.
